LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD calls `main` at the top level, which uses `eval` to dynamically generate `package_*` functions for each entry in `pkgname`. During `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, the PKGBUILD is sourced and `main` executes, but it only defines functions — it does not invoke `_package` or perform file installations. The `eval` constructs function bodies containing a command substitution `$(echo ${_pkgname%-*} | sed ...)` that extracts a model identifier from the hardcoded package name (e.g., `b7402`, `e210ma`). This substitution runs during the eval, but it only produces harmless string values used for `sed` replacements later during actual packaging. No network requests, data exfiltration, or execution of untrusted code occurs during sourcing. The `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, and `_package()` functions are defined but not executed during `--printsrcinfo`, so their contents (including `patch` and `install` commands) are out of scope for this gate.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
